biggest_catch: Long 13.5-hour Election Day workday at $15-$17/hour; drafted voters who fail to serve or attend training commit a Class V misdemeanor under Nebraska law.
catches: Election-day only work, not steady employment.
Long day: workers must be able to work a 13.5-hour workday (arrive by 7:00 a.m.; polls 8:00 a.m.-8:00 p.m.).
Training required before each and every election.
Registered voters may be drafted to serve (four elections of required service); drafted workers who fail to serve face a Class V misdemeanor.

steps: Be a registered voter in Douglas County, Nebraska (or at least 16 to serve as a clerk).
Respond to the Election Commission Selection Letter if chosen to work (volunteers may apply via the new-worker form).
Complete the required training before each election (online).
Arrive at the assigned polling place by 7:00 a.m. on Election Day and work the 13.5-hour day until all duties are complete.
timing: Election-day only; official 13.5-hour workday (arrive 7:00 a.m.; polls 8:00 a.m.-8:00 p.m.), plus required training before each election.
